name: writing-for-agents
description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
---

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** is the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** is the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types: **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand). The two mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** is the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** is consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung), which is a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** is pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent. Grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity**: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead (the **post-completion steps**) supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence. Hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand**: how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** (the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step), and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence**: split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation**, skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors: you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea. Each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_, turning a fuzzy gate into a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire. Go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive**: state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** (the same meaning in more than one place) costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too (`package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output), and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test (does it change behaviour versus the default?) is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

MANIFEST = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "artifacts/runs/review-20261017033849Z/sources.json"
SUBJECTS = ["claim:C08:1", "claim:C01:1", "permit:P122:1"]


def clear_work(key):
    return Work(key, tuple(Check(domain, True, "Required fact verified", "owner", "Continue within scope", ("source:record",)) for domain in sorted(DOMAINS)))


def held_work(key, domain="evidence"):
    work = clear_work(key)
    return replace(work, checks=tuple(replace(check, satisfied=False) if check.domain == domain else check for check in work.checks))


class DependencyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_unrelated_work_continues_and_real_dependency_propagates(self):
        blocked = held_work("evidence-A")
        dependent = replace(clear_work("claim-B"), dependencies=(Dependency("evidence-A", "Needs the same unresolved payment proof", "receipt:A"),))
        downstream = replace(clear_work("claim-C"), dependencies=(Dependency("claim-B", "Needs its verified obligation", "request:B"),))
        result = evaluate([blocked, dependent, downstream, clear_work("claim-D")])
        self.assertFalse(result["evidence-A"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertFalse(result["claim-B"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertFalse(result["claim-C"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertTrue(result["claim-D"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertEqual(result["claim-B"]["holds"][0]["prerequisite"], "evidence-A")

    def test_shared_reviewer_or_source_is_not_an_edge(self):
        result = evaluate([held_work("claim-A"), clear_work("claim-B")])
        self.assertTrue(result["claim-B"]["may_continue"])

    def test_missing_dependency_and_cycle_are_owned_holds(self):
        a = replace(clear_work("A"), dependencies=(Dependency("B", "Dependent authorization", "decision:1"),))
        self.assertFalse(evaluate([a])["A"]["may_continue"])
        b = replace(clear_work("B"), dependencies=(Dependency("A", "Dependent evidence", "decision:2"),))
        result = evaluate([a, b, clear_work("C")])
        self.assertFalse(result["A"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertFalse(result["B"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertTrue(result["C"]["may_continue"])

    def test_missing_domain_never_proves_independence(self):
        work = clear_work("A")
        work = replace(work, checks=tuple(c for c in work.checks if c.domain != "obligations"))
        self.assertFalse(evaluate([work])["A"]["may_continue"])

    def test_explicit_held_authority_or_budget_only_affects_dependents(self):
        for domain in ["authority", "budget", "obligations"]:
            with self.subTest(domain=domain):
                dependent = replace(clear_work("B"), dependencies=(Dependency("A", "Actual shared prerequisite", "source:shared-fact"),))
                result = evaluate([held_work("A", domain), dependent, clear_work("C")])
                self.assertFalse(result["B"]["may_continue"])
                self.assertTrue(result["C"]["may_continue"])

    def test_arrival_precedes_joins_even_if_rows_are_out_of_order(self):
        rows = [{"Arrival batch": 2, "event": "settled"}, {"Arrival batch": 1, "event": "accepted"}]
        self.assertEqual([r["event"] for r in visible_at(rows, 1)], ["accepted"])
        self.assertEqual(len(visible_at(rows, 2)), 2)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            visible_at([{"Arrival batch": None}], 1)


class BudgetTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):

    def test_prior_settled_portion_is_not_subtracted_twice(self):

class DependencyTests(unittest.TestCase):

        blocked = held_work("evidence-A")

        self.assertFalse(result["evidence-A"]["may_continue"])

        self.assertFalse(result["claim-C"]["may_continue"])
        self.assertTrue(result["claim-D"]["may_continue"])

    def test_shared_reviewer_or_source_is_not_an_edge(self):

"""Pure per-line arithmetic; evidence, exception authority and eligibility are external.

Amounts use Decimal throughout and each converted line is rounded half-up once.
An unresolved calculation returns ``allowed_cents=None``, never an invented zero.
Informational findings have ``blocking=False``; original cap findings survive a
caller-validated replacement. A replacement does not resolve an undefined cap
in this component: that would need an explicit additional source rule.
"""

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, localcontext
import re


KNOWN_CATEGORIES = frozenset({"transport", "conference", "lodging", "meals", "personal"})


def _decimal(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None:
        raise ValueError("Expected a finite decimal number")
    try:
        number = Decimal(str(value))
    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) as error:
        raise ValueError("Expected a finite decimal number") from error
    if not number.is_finite():
        raise ValueError("Expected a finite decimal number")
    return number


def _day(value):
    if type(value) is date:
        return value
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", value):
        raise ValueError("Expected a local YYYY-MM-DD date")
    return date.fromisoformat(value)


def _text(value):
    text = format(value, "f")
    return (text.rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if "." in text else text) if value else "0"


def _precision(*values):
    return max(50, sum(len(v.as_tuple().digits) + abs(v.as_tuple().exponent) for v in values) + 10)


def calculate_line(*, gross, currency, category, units, destination, payment_date,
                   fx_rows, caps_rows, replacement_allowed=None):
    """Calculate one supported line using native table headings and ``_ref``.

    The caller must establish paid evidence and validate any Finance replacement's
    actor, claim/revision, cost and scope. This function grants no eligibility
    waiver, approval, request authority or closure. ``allowed_original`` remains
    available when only FX is unresolved; ``rate=None`` on a foreign personal
    purchase means conversion is unnecessary because its known entitlement is 0.
    """
    result = dict(allowed_cents=None, allowed_original=None, rate=None,
                  findings=[], source_refs=[])

    def finding(code, detail, *, blocking=True, **facts):
        result["findings"].append(dict(code=code, detail=detail, blocking=blocking, **facts))

    def refs(rows, complete=None):
        for row in rows:
            reference = row.get("_ref")
            if reference and reference not in result["source_refs"]:
                result["source_refs"].append(reference)
        if complete and complete not in result["source_refs"]:
            result["source_refs"].append(complete)

    try:
        gross_amount, unit_count = _decimal(gross), _decimal(units)
        paid_on = _day(payment_date)
        if gross_amount < 0 or unit_count <= 0 or unit_count != unit_count.to_integral_value():
            raise ValueError("Gross must be nonnegative and units a positive integer")
        if not isinstance(currency, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{3}", currency):
            raise ValueError("Currency must be an explicit three-letter code")
        replacement = None if replacement_allowed is None else _decimal(replacement_allowed)
        if replacement is not None and replacement < 0:
            raise ValueError("Replacement allowed amount must be nonnegative")
    except ValueError as error:
        finding("invalid_input", str(error))
        return result

    if category not in KNOWN_CATEGORIES:
        finding("unknown_category", "No supplied arithmetic rule for category: " + str(category))
        return result
    if category == "personal":
        result.update(allowed_cents=0, allowed_original="0", rate="1" if currency == "EUR" else None)
        finding("personal_excluded", "Personal purchases have known zero entitlement", blocking=False)
        return result

    ordinary_allowed = gross_amount
    if category in {"lodging", "meals"}:
        candidates = [row for row in caps_rows if row.get("Destination") == destination
                      and row.get("Category") == category and row.get("Currency") == currency]
        matching = []
        for row in candidates:
            try:
                start, end = _day(row.get("Effective from")), _day(row.get("Effective to"))
                if end < start:
                    raise ValueError("Cap effective period ends before it starts")
            except ValueError as error:
                refs([row])
                finding("invalid_cap", str(error))
                return result
            if start <= paid_on <= end:
                matching.append(row)
        refs(matching)
        if len(matching) != 1:
            refs(candidates, "REGISTERS-CAPS:complete-tab")
            finding("missing_cap" if not matching else "ambiguous_cap",
                    "Need exactly one applicable destination/category/currency/payment-date cap")
            return result
        try:
            cap = _decimal(matching[0].get("Amount per unit"))
            if cap < 0:
                raise ValueError("Cap cannot be negative")
        except ValueError as error:
            finding("invalid_cap", str(error))
            return result
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = _precision(gross_amount, cap, unit_count)
            limit = cap * unit_count
            ordinary_allowed = min(gross_amount, limit)
        if ordinary_allowed < gross_amount:
            finding("cap_applied", "Ordinary allowed amount is limited by the applicable cap and units",
                    blocking=False, gross_original=_text(gross_amount), cap_total_original=_text(limit),
                    ordinary_allowed_original=_text(ordinary_allowed))

    allowed = ordinary_allowed if replacement is None else replacement
    if replacement is not None:
        finding("replacement_applied", "Caller-validated replacement controls the allowed original amount",
                blocking=False, ordinary_allowed_original=_text(ordinary_allowed),
                replacement_allowed_original=_text(replacement))
    result["allowed_original"] = _text(allowed)

    if currency == "EUR":
        rate = Decimal(1)
    else:
        candidates = [row for row in fx_rows if row.get("Currency") == currency]
        matching = []
        for row in candidates:
            try:
                rate_day = _day(row.get("Rate date"))
            except ValueError as error:
                refs([row])
                finding("invalid_rate", str(error))
                return result
            if rate_day == paid_on:
                matching.append(row)
        refs(matching)
        if len(matching) != 1:
            refs(candidates, "REGISTERS-FX:complete-tab")
            finding("missing_rate" if not matching else "ambiguous_rate",
                    "Need exactly one exact payment-date rate for the expense currency")
            return result
        try:
            rate = _decimal(matching[0].get("EUR per currency unit"))
            if rate <= 0:
                raise ValueError("Exchange rate must be positive")
        except ValueError as error:
            finding("invalid_rate", str(error))
            return result
    with localcontext() as context:
        context.prec = _precision(allowed, rate)
        converted = (allowed * rate).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
        result["allowed_cents"] = int(converted * 100)
    result["rate"] = _text(rate)
    return result

from decimal import Decimal
import unittest

from travel_expense_claim.monetary import calculate_line


FX = [{"Rate reference": "FX-USD", "Rate date": "2026-09-01", "Currency": "USD",
       "EUR per currency unit": Decimal("0.9"), "_ref": "REGISTERS-FX:row7"}]
CAPS = [
    {"Cap reference": "CAP-lodging", "Destination": "NL", "Category": "lodging", "Currency": "EUR",
     "Effective from": "2026-01-01", "Effective to": "2026-12-31", "Amount per unit": Decimal("150"), "_ref": "REGISTERS-CAPS:row6"},
    {"Cap reference": "CAP-meals", "Destination": "NL", "Category": "meals", "Currency": "EUR",
     "Effective from": "2026-01-01", "Effective to": "2026-12-31", "Amount per unit": Decimal("40"), "_ref": "REGISTERS-CAPS:row7"},
]


def line(**changes):
    values = dict(gross=Decimal("80"), currency="EUR", category="transport", units=1,
                  destination="NL", payment_date="2026-09-01", fx_rows=FX, caps_rows=CAPS)
    values.update(changes)
    return calculate_line(**values)


def codes(result):
    return {finding["code"] for finding in result["findings"]}


class MonetaryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_provided_c09_and_c19_values_and_replacement(self):
        self.assertEqual(line()["allowed_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual(line(gross="100")["allowed_cents"], 10000)
        corrected = line(gross="100", replacement_allowed="80")
        self.assertEqual(corrected["allowed_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual(corrected["allowed_original"], "80")
        self.assertEqual(corrected["rate"], "1")
        self.assertEqual(corrected["findings"][0]["ordinary_allowed_original"], "100")

    def test_finance_replacement_has_no_invented_paid_gross_upper_bound(self):
        self.assertEqual(line(gross="80", replacement_allowed="90")["allowed_cents"], 9000)
        for amount in ["-1", "NaN", "Infinity"]:
            with self.subTest(amount=amount):
                self.assertIsNone(line(replacement_allowed=amount)["allowed_cents"])

    def test_transport_conference_threshold_values_are_not_caps(self):
        for category in ["transport", "conference"]:
            for gross, expected in [("999.99", 99999), ("1000.00", 100000), ("1000.01", 100001)]:
                with self.subTest(category=category, gross=gross):
                    self.assertEqual(line(category=category, gross=gross)["allowed_cents"], expected)

    def test_lodging_meal_cap_boundaries_and_units(self):
        for category, amounts in [("lodging", [("149.99", 14999), ("150", 15000), ("150.01", 15000)]),
                                  ("meals", [("39.99", 3999), ("40", 4000), ("40.01", 4000)])]:
            for gross, expected in amounts:
                with self.subTest(category=category, gross=gross):
                    self.assertEqual(line(category=category, gross=gross)["allowed_cents"], expected)
        self.assertEqual(line(category="lodging", gross="360", units=2)["allowed_cents"], 30000)

    def test_cap_uses_original_currency_destination_and_inclusive_payment_date(self):
        for paid in ["2026-01-01", "2026-12-31"]:
            self.assertEqual(line(category="lodging", gross="200", payment_date=paid)["allowed_cents"], 15000)
        for change in [dict(destination="BE"), dict(currency="USD"), dict(payment_date="2027-01-01")]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                result = line(category="lodging", gross="200", **change)
                self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
                self.assertIn("missing_cap", codes(result))
        usd_cap = {**CAPS[0], "Currency": "USD", "Amount per unit": Decimal("50")}
        result = line(category="lodging", currency="USD", gross="100", caps_rows=[usd_cap])
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 4500)
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_original"], "50")

    def test_missing_ambiguous_cap_never_becomes_zero_even_with_replacement(self):
        for rows, code in [([], "missing_cap"), ([CAPS[0], CAPS[0]], "ambiguous_cap")]:
            result = line(category="lodging", caps_rows=rows, replacement_allowed="20")
            self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
            self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_original"])
            self.assertIn(code, codes(result))

    def test_original_cap_finding_survives_replacement(self):
        result = line(category="lodging", gross="200", replacement_allowed="180")
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 18000)
        self.assertEqual(codes(result), {"cap_applied", "replacement_applied"})
        self.assertTrue(all(not f["blocking"] for f in result["findings"]))
        self.assertIn("REGISTERS-CAPS:row6", result["source_refs"])

    def test_eur_zero_personal_zero_and_unknown_are_distinct(self):
        self.assertEqual(line(gross=0, fx_rows=[])["allowed_cents"], 0)
        personal = line(category="personal", currency="GBP", fx_rows=[])
        self.assertEqual(personal["allowed_cents"], 0)
        self.assertIsNone(personal["rate"])
        self.assertIn("personal_excluded", codes(personal))
        unknown = line(category="entertainment", gross=0, replacement_allowed=0)
        self.assertIsNone(unknown["allowed_cents"])
        self.assertIn("unknown_category", codes(unknown))

    def test_fx_needs_unique_exact_payment_date_currency_and_positive_value(self):
        result = line(currency="USD", gross="600")
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 54000)
        self.assertEqual(result["rate"], "0.9")
        self.assertEqual(result["source_refs"], ["REGISTERS-FX:row7"])
        for change in [dict(currency="GBP"), dict(payment_date="2026-09-02"), dict(fx_rows=[])]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                result = line(**{"currency": "USD", **change})
                self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
                self.assertIn("missing_rate", codes(result))
                self.assertIsNotNone(result["allowed_original"])
        result = line(currency="USD", fx_rows=FX * 2)
        self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
        self.assertIn("ambiguous_rate", codes(result))
        for rate in ["0", "-1", "NaN", "Infinity"]:
            with self.subTest(rate=rate):
                self.assertIn("invalid_rate", codes(line(currency="USD", fx_rows=[{**FX[0], "EUR per currency unit": rate}])))

    def test_half_up_happens_per_line_before_summing(self):
        lines = [line(currency="USD", gross="1.15", category=category) for category in ["transport", "conference"]]
        self.assertEqual([r["allowed_cents"] for r in lines], [104, 104])
        self.assertEqual(sum(r["allowed_cents"] for r in lines), 208)
        self.assertEqual(line(currency="USD", gross="2.30")["allowed_cents"], 207)
        self.assertEqual([line(currency="USD", gross="1.16")["allowed_cents"] for _ in range(2)], [104, 104])

    def test_invalid_inputs_and_definitions_remain_unresolved(self):
        for change in [dict(gross="-1"), dict(gross="NaN"), dict(units=0), dict(units="1.5"),
                       dict(units=True), dict(currency="eur"), dict(payment_date="2026-02-30")]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                self.assertIn("invalid_input", codes(line(**change)))
        for field, value in [("Amount per unit", "-1"), ("Effective from", "bad-date"), ("Effective to", "2025-01-01")]:
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                self.assertIn("invalid_cap", codes(line(category="lodging", caps_rows=[{**CAPS[0], field: value}])))
        self.assertIn("invalid_rate", codes(line(currency="USD", fx_rows=[{**FX[0], "Rate date": "bad-date"}])))

    def test_inputs_are_not_mutated_and_decimal_precision_is_preserved(self):
        caps, fx = deepcopy(CAPS), deepcopy(FX)
        before = deepcopy((caps, fx))
        result = line(currency="USD", gross="123456789012345678901234567890.15", caps_rows=caps, fx_rows=fx)
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 11111111011111111101111111110114)
        self.assertEqual((caps, fx), before)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

            finding("missing_rate" if not matching else "ambiguous_rate",
                    "Need exactly one exact payment-date rate for the expense currency")
            return result
        try:
            rate = _decimal(matching[0].get("EUR per currency unit"))
            if rate <= 0:
                raise ValueError("Exchange rate must be positive")
        except ValueError as error:
            finding("invalid_rate", str(error))
            return result
    with localcontext() as context:
        context.prec = _precision(allowed, rate)
        converted = (allowed * rate).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

from travel_expense_claim.monetary import calculate_line


FX = [{"Rate reference": "FX-USD", "Rate date": "2026-09-01", "Currency": "USD",

     "Effective from": "2026-01-01", "Effective to": "2026-12-31", "Amount per unit": Decimal("40"), "_ref": "REGISTERS-CAPS:row7"},
]


def line(**changes):
    values = dict(gross=Decimal("80"), currency="EUR", category="transport", units=1,
                  destination="NL", payment_date="2026-09-01", fx_rows=FX, caps_rows=CAPS)
    values.update(changes)
    return calculate_line(**values)


def codes(result):
    return {finding["code"] for finding in result["findings"]}


class MonetaryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_provided_c09_and_c19_values_and_replacement(self):
        self.assertEqual(line()["allowed_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual(line(gross="100")["allowed_cents"], 10000)
        corrected = line(gross="100", replacement_allowed="80")
        self.assertEqual(corrected["allowed_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual(corrected["allowed_original"], "80")
        self.assertEqual(corrected["rate"], "1")
        self.assertEqual(corrected["findings"][0]["ordinary_allowed_original"], "100")

    def test_finance_replacement_has_no_invented_paid_gross_upper_bound(self):
        self.assertEqual(line(gross="80", replacement_allowed="90")["allowed_cents"], 9000)
        for amount in ["-1", "NaN", "Infinity"]:
            with self.subTest(amount=amount):
                self.assertIsNone(line(replacement_allowed=amount)["allowed_cents"])

    def test_transport_conference_threshold_values_are_not_caps(self):
        for category in ["transport", "conference"]:
            for gross, expected in [("999.99", 99999), ("1000.00", 100000), ("1000.01", 100001)]:
                with self.subTest(category=category, gross=gross):
                    self.assertEqual(line(category=category, gross=gross)["allowed_cents"], expected)

    def test_lodging_meal_cap_boundaries_and_units(self):
        for category, amounts in [("lodging", [("149.99", 14999), ("150", 15000), ("150.01", 15000)]),
                                  ("meals", [("39.99", 3999), ("40", 4000), ("40.01", 4000)])]:
            for gross, expected in amounts:
                with self.subTest(category=category, gross=gross):
                    self.assertEqual(line(category=category, gross=gross)["allowed_cents"], expected)
        self.assertEqual(line(category="lodging", gross="360", units=2)["allowed_cents"], 30000)

    def test_cap_uses_original_currency_destination_and_inclusive_payment_date(self):
        for paid in ["2026-01-01", "2026-12-31"]:
            self.assertEqual(line(category="lodging", gross="200", payment_date=paid)["allowed_cents"], 15000)
        for change in [dict(destination="BE"), dict(currency="USD"), dict(payment_date="2027-01-01")]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                result = line(category="lodging", gross="200", **change)
                self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
                self.assertIn("missing_cap", codes(result))
        usd_cap = {**CAPS[0], "Currency": "USD", "Amount per unit": Decimal("50")}
        result = line(category="lodging", currency="USD", gross="100", caps_rows=[usd_cap])
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 4500)
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_original"], "50")

    def test_missing_ambiguous_cap_never_becomes_zero_even_with_replacement(self):
        for rows, code in [([], "missing_cap"), ([CAPS[0], CAPS[0]], "ambiguous_cap")]:
            result = line(category="lodging", caps_rows=rows, replacement_allowed="20")
            self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
            self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_original"])
            self.assertIn(code, codes(result))

    def test_original_cap_finding_survives_replacement(self):
        result = line(category="lodging", gross="200", replacement_allowed="180")
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 18000)
        self.assertEqual(codes(result), {"cap_applied", "replacement_applied"})
        self.assertTrue(all(not f["blocking"] for f in result["findings"]))
        self.assertIn("REGISTERS-CAPS:row6", result["source_refs"])

    def test_eur_zero_personal_zero_and_unknown_are_distinct(self):
        self.assertEqual(line(gross=0, fx_rows=[])["allowed_cents"], 0)
        personal = line(category="personal", currency="GBP", fx_rows=[])
        self.assertEqual(personal["allowed_cents"], 0)
        self.assertIsNone(personal["rate"])
        self.assertIn("personal_excluded", codes(personal))
        unknown = line(category="entertainment", gross=0, replacement_allowed=0)
        self.assertIsNone(unknown["allowed_cents"])
        self.assertIn("unknown_category", codes(unknown))

    def test_fx_needs_unique_exact_payment_date_currency_and_positive_value(self):
        result = line(currency="USD", gross="600")
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 54000)
        self.assertEqual(result["rate"], "0.9")
        self.assertEqual(result["source_refs"], ["REGISTERS-FX:row7"])
        for change in [dict(currency="GBP"), dict(payment_date="2026-09-02"), dict(fx_rows=[])]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                result = line(**{"currency": "USD", **change})
                self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
                self.assertIn("missing_rate", codes(result))
                self.assertIsNotNone(result["allowed_original"])
        result = line(currency="USD", fx_rows=FX * 2)
        self.assertIsNone(result["allowed_cents"])
        self.assertIn("ambiguous_rate", codes(result))
        for rate in ["0", "-1", "NaN", "Infinity"]:
            with self.subTest(rate=rate):
                self.assertIn("invalid_rate", codes(line(currency="USD", fx_rows=[{**FX[0], "EUR per currency unit": rate}])))

    def test_half_up_happens_per_line_before_summing(self):
        lines = [line(currency="USD", gross="1.15", category=category) for category in ["transport", "conference"]]
        self.assertEqual([r["allowed_cents"] for r in lines], [104, 104])
        self.assertEqual(sum(r["allowed_cents"] for r in lines), 208)
        self.assertEqual(line(currency="USD", gross="2.30")["allowed_cents"], 207)
        self.assertEqual([line(currency="USD", gross="1.16")["allowed_cents"] for _ in range(2)], [104, 104])

    def test_invalid_inputs_and_definitions_remain_unresolved(self):
        for change in [dict(gross="-1"), dict(gross="NaN"), dict(units=0), dict(units="1.5"),
                       dict(units=True), dict(currency="eur"), dict(payment_date="2026-02-30")]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                self.assertIn("invalid_input", codes(line(**change)))
        for field, value in [("Amount per unit", "-1"), ("Effective from", "bad-date"), ("Effective to", "2025-01-01")]:
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                self.assertIn("invalid_cap", codes(line(category="lodging", caps_rows=[{**CAPS[0], field: value}])))
        self.assertIn("invalid_rate", codes(line(currency="USD", fx_rows=[{**FX[0], "Rate date": "bad-date"}])))

    def test_inputs_are_not_mutated_and_decimal_precision_is_preserved(self):
        caps, fx = deepcopy(CAPS), deepcopy(FX)
        before = deepcopy((caps, fx))
        result = line(currency="USD", gross="123456789012345678901234567890.15", caps_rows=caps, fx_rows=fx)
        self.assertEqual(result["allowed_cents"], 11111111011111111101111111110114)
        self.assertEqual((caps, fx), before)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

                raise SourceError("Missing or repeated expense line in claim version")
            item = dict(id=field(text, "Claim reference"), revision=int(field(text, "Revision")),
                        batch=int(field(text, "Arrival batch")), employee=field(text, "Employee"),
                        trip=field(text, "Trip reference"), trip_revision=int(field(text, "Trip revision")),
                        submitted=field(text, "Submitted date"), status=field(text, "Status"),
                        reason=field(text, "Claim reason"), lines=lines, exception=None,
                        source_ref=f"{reference}:page{page['page']}")
            if "Authorizing Finance officer:" in text:
                reason = re.search(r"Exception reason:\s*(.*?)(?=\n\s*\n|\Z)", text, re.S)
                if not reason:
                    raise SourceError("Finance exception needs a reason")
                raw_issues = field(text, "Covered issues")
                words = [value.strip().lower().replace("_", " ") for value in re.split(r"[,;]", raw_issues)]
                item["exception"] = dict(actor=field(text, "Authorizing Finance officer"),
                    claim_id=field(text, "Applies to claim"), revision=int(field(text, "Applies to revision")),
                    cost_id=field(text, "Expense reference"), allowed=Decimal(field(text, "Allowed original amount")),
                    covered_issues=[] if words == ["none"] else [ISSUE_NAMES.get(value, value) for value in words],
                    cancellation_id=field(text, "Travel cancellation reference") if "Travel cancellation reference:" in text else None,
                    reason=" ".join(reason.group(1).split()), source_ref=item["source_ref"])
            key = (item["id"], item["revision"])
            if key in seen or item["batch"] < 1 or item["revision"] < 1:
                raise SourceError("Invalid or ambiguous claim version")
            seen.add(key)
            result.append(item)
    return result


def receipts_with_metadata(sources):
    result = receipt_records(sources)
    for page in sources.read("RECEIPTS-PAGES"):
        for block in re.split(r"(?=Receipt reference:)", page["text"])[1:]:
            result[field(block, "Receipt reference")].update(
                category=field(block, "Category"), units=field(block, "Documented units"),
                issued=field(block, "Issued date"))
    return result


def filing_deadline(end):
    original = date.fromisoformat(end)
    year, month = divmod(original.year * 12 + original.month - 1 + 2, 12)
    month += 1
    return date(year, month, min(original.day, monthrange(year, month)[1]))


def validate_exception(claim, line, person):
    exception = claim.get("exception")
    if not exception:
        return None, None
    valid = (exception["actor"] == person["Finance officer"]
             and exception["claim_id"] == claim["id"] and exception["revision"] == claim["revision"]
             and exception["cost_id"] == line["cost_id"] and bool(exception["reason"])
             and exception["allowed"].is_finite() and exception["allowed"] >= 0
             and set(exception["covered_issues"]) <= set(ISSUE_NAMES.values()))
    if not valid:
        return None, "Exception actor, revision, cost, amount, reason or covered issues do not bind this line"
    return exception, None


def material_changes(previous, current):
    if previous is None:
        return []
    fields = ("employee", "trip", "trip_revision", "submitted", "status", "lines")
    changes = [key for key in fields if previous[key] != current[key]]
    def exception_basis(claim):
        exception = claim.get("exception")
        return None if exception is None else {key: value for key, value in exception.items()
                                               if key not in {"revision", "source_ref"}}
    if exception_basis(previous) != exception_basis(current):
        changes.append("Finance exception basis")
    return changes


def budget_context(person, ledger, finance, people):
    group = tuple(person[key] for key in ("Department", "Project", "Budget period"))
    rows = [row for row in ledger if tuple(row[key] for key in ("Department", "Project", "Budget period")) == group]
    available = budget_remaining(rows, [])
    charges, uncertainty = [], []
    prior_ids = {row["Obligation reference"] for row in rows if row["Entry type"] == "obligation"}
    for request_id, request in finance["requests"].items():
        owner = people[request["employee_id"]]
        if tuple(owner[key] for key in ("Department", "Project", "Budget period")) != group:
            continue
        if request_id in prior_ids:
            uncertainty.append("Accepted request also occurs in prior ledger: " + request_id)
            continue
        # Paid money remains expenditure even when a corrected obligation is lower.
        charge = max(request["current_obligation_cents"], request["net_paid_cents"])
        charges.append(dict(request_id=request_id, charged_cents=charge,
                            obligation_cents=request["current_obligation_cents"],
                            net_paid_cents=request["net_paid_cents"], source_refs=request["source_refs"]))
        if available is not None:
            available -= charge
    for issue in finance["rejected_events"]:
        if issue["code"] not in {"invalid_refund_link", "refund_exceeds_transfer", "invalid_retry"}:
            # An untrusted acceptance/adjustment could hide a shared commitment.
            matching = [r for r in ledger if r.get("_ref") in issue["source_refs"]]
            if matching:
                uncertainty.append(issue["reason"])
    return dict(group=list(group), remaining_cents=available,
                sufficient=available is not None and available >= 0 and not uncertainty,
                uncertainty=uncertainty, charges=charges,
                source_refs=[row["_ref"] for row in rows])


def _recheck(claim, history, sources, tables, receipts, reviews, packets, cancellations, finance):
    person = tables["people"][claim["employee"]]
    trip = single([row for row in tables["Trips"] if row["Trip reference"] == claim["trip"]
                   and row["Trip revision"] == claim["trip_revision"]], "current trip revision")
    issues, lines = [], []
    def issue(code, detail, owner, refs, *, resolved_by=None, next_action=None):
        item = dict(code=code, detail=detail, owner=owner, source_refs=sorted(set(refs)),
                    resolved_by=resolved_by, blocking=resolved_by is None,
                    next_action=next_action or "Obtain source-bound current evidence or applicable human response")
        issues.append(item)
        return item
    if trip["Employee ID"] != claim["employee"]:
        issue("trip_identity", "Trip employee does not match current claim", claim["employee"], [trip["_ref"], claim["source_ref"]])
    if trip["International"]:
        issue("permit_review_pending", "This scoped recheck has not implemented international permit eligibility", person["Administration reviewer"], [trip["_ref"], "POLICY:paragraph4"])
    relevant = [process for process in cancellations["processes"] if process["trip"] == claim["trip"]
                and process["trip_revision"] == claim["trip_revision"]]
    confirmed = [process for process in relevant if process["status"] == "confirmed"]
    for process in relevant:
        if process["status"] == "requested":
            issue("cancellation_pending", "A valid business cancellation request pauses affected payment readiness", person["Supervisor"], process["source_refs"])
    for hold in cancellations["holds"]:
        if hold.get("trip") == claim["trip"]:
            issue("cancellation_import", hold.get("reason", str(hold)), person["Supervisor"], hold["source_refs"])
    previous_costs = {}
    for old in history:
        if old["revision"] < claim["revision"]:
            for line in old["lines"]:
                previous_costs.setdefault(line["cost_id"], line["first_submitted"])
    for line in claim["lines"]:
        receipt = receipts.get(line["receipt_id"])
        check = payment_check(claim, line, receipt, tables["Merchant payments"], sources.data["case_clock"])
        exception, exception_error = validate_exception(claim, line, person)
        if exception_error:
            issue("invalid_exception", exception_error, person["Finance officer"], [claim["source_ref"]])
        calculation = dict(allowed_cents=None, findings=[], source_refs=[])
        settled = [row for row in tables["Merchant payments"] if row["_ref"] in check.source_refs]
        if not check.satisfied:
            issue("paid_evidence", check.fact, claim["employee"], check.source_refs, next_action=check.next_action)
        else:
            paid = single(settled, "matching paid proof")
            first = previous_costs.get(line["cost_id"], line["first_submitted"])
            if first != line["first_submitted"]:
                issue("changed_first_filing", "Unchanged cost cannot reset its initial filing date", person["Administration reviewer"], [claim["source_ref"], *[v["source_ref"] for v in history]])
            if date.fromisoformat(first) < date.fromisoformat(paid["Paid date"]) or date.fromisoformat(first) < date.fromisoformat(receipt["issued"]):
                issue("filing_before_evidence", "Initial filing predates payment or receipt", claim["employee"], check.source_refs)
            if date.fromisoformat(first) > filing_deadline(trip["End date"]):
                resolved = exception["source_ref"] if exception and "late_filing" in exception["covered_issues"] else None
                issue("late_filing", "First filing is after the original planned trip deadline", person["Finance officer"], [claim["source_ref"], trip["_ref"]], resolved_by=resolved)
            calculation = calculate_line(gross=line["gross"], currency=line["currency"], category=receipt["category"],
                units=receipt["units"], destination=trip["Destination"], payment_date=paid["Paid date"],
                fx_rows=tables["FX"], caps_rows=tables["Caps"], replacement_allowed=exception["allowed"] if exception else None)
            for finding in calculation["findings"]:
                if finding["blocking"]:
                    issue(finding["code"], finding["detail"], person["Finance officer"], [*check.source_refs, *calculation["source_refs"]])
        for process in confirmed:
            resolved = (exception["source_ref"] if exception and "travel_cancellation" in exception["covered_issues"]
                        and exception["cancellation_id"] == process["cancellation_id"] else None)
            issue("travel_cancellation", f"{line['cost_id']} needs explicit cost disposition for {process['cancellation_id']}",
                  person["Finance officer"], [claim["source_ref"], *process["source_refs"]], resolved_by=resolved)
            if settled and settled[0]["Paid date"] == process["confirmed_time"][:10]:
                issue("cancellation_payment_order", "Date-only payment and same-day cancellation have unresolved ordering", person["Finance officer"], [*check.source_refs, *process["source_refs"]])
        lines.append(dict(cost_id=line["cost_id"], receipt_id=line["receipt_id"], evidence_supported=check.satisfied,
                          first_filed=previous_costs.get(line["cost_id"], line["first_submitted"]),
                          filing_deadline=filing_deadline(trip["End date"]).isoformat(),
                          calculation=calculation, exception=exception, source_refs=list(check.source_refs)))
    entitlement = None if any(line["calculation"]["allowed_cents"] is None for line in lines) else sum(line["calculation"]["allowed_cents"] for line in lines)
    authority = recheck_authority(claim, trip, person, entitlement, reviews, packets, relevant, sources)
    if not authority["current"]:
        issue("current_approvals", "Current revision lacks applicable approval roles: " + ", ".join(authority["missing_roles"]), person["Administration reviewer"], authority["source_refs"] or [claim["source_ref"]])
    current_finance = finance["claims"][claim["id"]]
    requests = [finance["requests"][key] for key in current_finance["request_ids"]]
    changes = material_changes(history[-2] if len(history) > 1 else None, claim)
    # Finance has no claim-revision field. Arrival context establishes whether its
    # first acceptance existed before the material correction became available.
    accepted_events = [event for event in finance["admitted_events"] if event["claim_id"] == claim["id"] and event["type"] == "accepted"]
    accepted_before_revision = any(next(row["Arrival batch"] for row in tables["visible_finance"]
        if row["Activity reference"] == event["event_id"]) < claim["batch"] for event in accepted_events)
    cancelled_after_acceptance = any(event["time"] < process["confirmed_time"] for event in accepted_events for process in confirmed)
    resolution_required = bool((changes and accepted_before_revision) or cancelled_after_acceptance
                               or any(event["claim_id"] == claim["id"] and event["type"] == "adjustment" for event in finance["admitted_events"]))
    # Resolution is current only if observed in/after this revision's batch, after
    # cancellation, and agreeing with both the corrected amount and obligation.
    resolutions = []
    for event in finance["admitted_events"]:
        if event["claim_id"] != claim["id"] or event["type"] != "resolution" or event["obligation_cents"] != entitlement:
            continue
        arrival = min(row["Arrival batch"] for row in tables["visible_finance"] if row["Activity reference"] == event["event_id"])
        if arrival >= claim["batch"] and all(event["time"] >= process["confirmed_time"] for process in confirmed):
            resolutions.append(event["event_id"])
    if resolution_required and not resolutions:
        issue("finance_resolution", "Post-acceptance material correction/cancellation needs current explicit Finance resolution", person["Finance officer"], [claim["source_ref"], *[ref for req in requests for ref in req["source_refs"]]])
    for hold in current_finance["holds"]:
        issue(hold["code"], hold["reason"], hold["owner"], hold["source_refs"])
    if requests and entitlement is not None and current_finance["current_obligation_cents"] != entitlement:
        issue("obligation_mismatch", "Recorded Finance obligation differs from rechecked amount", person["Finance officer"], [claim["source_ref"], *[ref for req in requests for ref in req["source_refs"]]])
    balance = None if entitlement is None else entitlement - current_finance["net_paid_cents"]
    if balance is not None and balance < 0:
        issue("overpayment", "Confirmed net paid exceeds current calculated amount; retain transfers until a linked refund", person["Finance officer"], [ref for req in requests for ref in req["source_refs"]])
    own_costs = {line["cost_id"] for line in claim["lines"]}
    shared = []
    for request_id, request in finance["requests"].items():
        if request["claim_id"] == claim["id"]:
            continue
        other_costs = {line["cost_id"] for version in tables["visible_versions"] if version["id"] == request["claim_id"] for line in version["lines"]}
        if own_costs & other_costs:
            shared.append(request_id)
            issue("shared_cost_obligation", "Cost is already bound to another accepted request: " + request_id,
                  person["Finance officer"], [claim["source_ref"], *request["source_refs"]])
    budget = budget_context(person, tables["Budget"], finance, tables["people"])
    if not budget["sufficient"]:
        issue("shared_budget", "Actual shared funding is deficient or unresolved", person["Budget owner"], budget["source_refs"])
    blocking = [item for item in issues if item["blocking"]]
    return dict(revision=claim["revision"], source_ref=claim["source_ref"], employee=claim["employee"], trip=claim["trip"],
        material_changes=changes, full_recheck_steps=["evidence", "calculations", "eligibility", "current approvals", "budget and obligations", "Finance history"],
        revision_history=[dict(revision=v["revision"], arrival_batch=v["batch"], source_ref=v["source_ref"], trip=v["trip"], employee=v["employee"]) for v in history],
        lines=lines, calculated_entitlement_cents=entitlement, issues=issues, authority=authority,
        finance=current_finance, original_requests={key: finance["requests"][key] for key in current_finance["request_ids"]},
        calculated_balance_cents=balance, finance_resolution_required=resolution_required, current_resolution_event_ids=resolutions,
        budget=budget, shared_cost_request_ids=shared, arrangements_paused=bool(relevant),
        trip_retired_for_future_arrangements=any(p["target_type"] == "trip" for p in confirmed),
        current_recheck_supported=not blocking, competing_replacement_requests_held=bool(accepted_before_revision and not resolutions),
        financial_completion_accepted=False, completion_choice="Learner choice 3 pending; no closure verdict",
        policy_refs=POLICY_REFS)


def inspect(manifest, claim_ids, through_batch=4):
    if not 1 <= through_batch <= 4 or not claim_ids or len(set(claim_ids)) != len(claim_ids):
        raise SourceError("Select distinct claim IDs and a batch from 1 through 4")
    sources = Sources(manifest)
    versions = claim_versions(sources)
    if not set(claim_ids) <= {claim["id"] for claim in versions}:
        raise SourceError("Requested claim not found in supplied versions")
    tables = {name: sources.table(name) for name in ("People", "Trips", "Merchant payments", "Budget", "FX", "Caps")}
    tables["people"] = {person["Employee ID"]: person for person in tables["People"]}
    # Effective cap dates are Excel calendar serials, not timestamps. Sources.table
    # exposes effectiveValue for these two headings; normalize from the native
    # serial without a timezone conversion.
    for cap in tables["Caps"]:
        for key in ("Effective from", "Effective to"):
            if isinstance(cap[key], (int, Decimal)):
                cap[key] = (date(1899, 12, 30) + timedelta(days=int(cap[key]))).isoformat()
    receipts = receipts_with_metadata(sources)
    all_reviews, all_packets = sources.table("Review ledger"), sources.table("Review packets")
    all_finance, all_cancellations = sources.table("Finance activity"), sources.table("Travel cancellations")
    batches = []
    for batch in range(1, through_batch + 1):
        visible = [claim for claim in versions if claim["batch"] <= batch]
        latest = {identity: max([v for v in visible if v["id"] == identity], key=lambda v: v["revision"])
                  for identity in {v["id"] for v in visible}}
        reviews = visible_at(all_reviews, batch)
        decision_ids = {row["Decision reference"] for row in reviews}
        packets = [packet for packet in all_packets if packet["Decision reference"] in decision_ids]
        tables["visible_versions"] = visible
        tables["visible_finance"] = visible_at(all_finance, batch)
        finance = summarize_finance(tables["visible_finance"], tables["people"], latest,
                                    sources.data["case_clock"], sources.data["case_timezone"])
        cancellation = reduce_cancellations(visible_at(all_cancellations, batch), tables["people"], tables["Trips"], sources)
        subjects = {}
        for identity in claim_ids:
            if identity not in latest:
                continue
            history = sorted([v for v in visible if v["id"] == identity], key=lambda v: v["revision"])
            subjects[identity] = _recheck(latest[identity], history, sources, tables, receipts, reviews, packets, cancellation, finance)
        batches.append(dict(batch_id=batch, claims=subjects, cancellation_processes=cancellation,
                            finance_replayed_event_ids=finance["replayed_event_ids"]))
    return dict(mode="offline retained-source full-recheck verification", scope="Current domestic claim rechecks; no dispatch, operational snapshot or completion acceptance",
        source_run_id=sources.data["run_id"], source_manifest_sha256=sha256(sources.path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        case_clock=sources.data["case_clock"], case_timezone=sources.data["case_timezone"], batches=batches)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--sources", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--claim", action="append", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--through-batch", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = inspect(args.sources, args.claim, args.through_batch)
    content = json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2, default=str) + "\n"
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if args.output.exists():
        if args.output.read_text() != content:
            raise SourceError("Distinct existing verification preserved; use a new output path")
    else:
        with args.output.open("x") as stream:
            stream.write(content)
    print(args.output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def event(identity, kind, batch, *, claim="A", request="REQ-A", amount=None,

class FullRecheckTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.result = inspect(MANIFEST, SUBJECTS)

    def at(self, batch, claim):
        return self.result["batches"][batch - 1]["claims"][claim]

    def test_c09_same_total_identity_change_rechecks_new_evidence_and_roles(self):
        old, current, settled = (self.at(batch, "C09") for batch in (1, 3, 4))
        self.assertEqual(old["calculated_entitlement_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertFalse(old["authority"]["current"])
        self.assertEqual(current["calculated_entitlement_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual(current["trip"], "T09B")
        self.assertEqual(current["lines"][0]["cost_id"], "COST-09B")
        self.assertEqual(set(current["material_changes"]), {"trip", "lines"})
        self.assertTrue(current["current_recheck_supported"])
        self.assertEqual(len(current["authority"]["valid_decision_ids"]), 3)
        self.assertEqual(current["finance"]["request_ids"], ["REQ-C09"])
        self.assertEqual(current["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 0)
        self.assertFalse(current["finance_resolution_required"])
        self.assertEqual(settled["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual([v["revision"] for v in settled["revision_history"]], [1, 2])

    def test_c19_amount_only_correction_preserves_payment_and_holds_cancellation(self):
        previous, current = (self.at(batch, "C19") for batch in (2, 3))
        self.assertEqual(previous["calculated_entitlement_cents"], 10000)
        self.assertEqual(previous["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 10000)
        self.assertEqual(current["revision"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(current["calculated_entitlement_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual(current["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 10000)
        self.assertEqual(current["calculated_balance_cents"], -2000)
        self.assertFalse(current["authority"]["current"])
        self.assertFalse(current["current_recheck_supported"])
        self.assertTrue(current["competing_replacement_requests_held"])
        codes = {item["code"] for item in current["issues"] if item["blocking"]}
        self.assertTrue({"travel_cancellation", "current_approvals", "finance_resolution", "overpayment"} <= codes)
        self.assertEqual(current["lines"][0]["exception"]["covered_issues"], [])

    def test_c19_current_revision_refund_resolution_and_reviews_agree_without_acceptance(self):
        current = self.at(4, "C19")
        self.assertEqual(current["revision"], 3)
        self.assertTrue(current["current_recheck_supported"])
        self.assertEqual(current["calculated_entitlement_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertEqual((current["finance"]["paid_cents"], current["finance"]["refunded_cents"], current["finance"]["net_paid_cents"]), (10000, 2000, 8000))
        self.assertEqual(current["calculated_balance_cents"], 0)
        self.assertTrue(current["finance_resolution_required"])
        self.assertEqual(current["current_resolution_event_ids"], ["F-C19-4"])
        self.assertEqual(current["finance"]["request_ids"], ["REQ-C19"])
        self.assertTrue(current["trip_retired_for_future_arrangements"])
        self.assertEqual([v["revision"] for v in current["revision_history"]], [1, 2, 3])
        self.assertFalse(current["financial_completion_accepted"])
        original = current["original_requests"]["REQ-C19"]
        self.assertEqual(original["initial_obligation_cents"], 10000)
        self.assertEqual(original["current_obligation_cents"], 8000)
        finding = next(item for item in current["issues"] if item["code"] == "travel_cancellation")
        self.assertEqual(finding["resolved_by"], "UPDATES:page7")
        self.assertIn("REGISTERS-TRAVEL-CANCELLATIONS:row13", finding["source_refs"])

    def test_batch_one_is_identical_to_replay_without_later_batches(self):
        early = inspect(MANIFEST, SUBJECTS, through_batch=1)
        self.assertEqual(early["batches"][0], self.result["batches"][0])
        self.assertEqual(self.at(1, "C19")["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.at(1, "C01")["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.at(1, "C01")["finance"]["admitted_event_ids"], ["F-C01-accepted"])
        self.assertEqual(self.at(1, "C09")["revision_history"], [dict(revision=1, arrival_batch=1, source_ref="INITIAL:page9", trip="T09", employee="EMP-01")])

    def test_independent_controls_and_no_claim_cancellation_remain_independent(self):
        for batch in range(1, 5):
            self.assertTrue(self.at(batch, "C01")["current_recheck_supported"])
            self.assertIsNone(self.at(batch, "C08")["calculated_entitlement_cents"])
            self.assertFalse(self.at(batch, "C08")["current_recheck_supported"])
            c08 = next(issue for issue in self.at(batch, "C08")["issues"] if issue["code"] == "paid_evidence")
            self.assertEqual(c08["owner"], "EMP-01")
            self.assertIn("R-COST-08", c08["next_action"])
        self.assertEqual(self.at(4, "C01")["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 10000)
        self.assertIn("F-C01-1", self.result["batches"][3]["finance_replayed_event_ids"])
        processes = self.result["batches"][3]["cancellation_processes"]["processes"]
        permit = next(process for process in processes if process["cancellation_id"] == "TC122")
        self.assertEqual(permit["status"], "confirmed")
        self.assertEqual(permit["permit"], "P122")
        self.assertNotIn("C122", self.result["batches"][3]["claims"])

    def test_shared_budget_charges_overpaid_c19_once_until_refund(self):
        for batch, charge in ((1, 10000), (2, 10000), (3, 10000), (4, 8000)):
            budget = self.at(batch, "C01")["budget"]
            self.assertTrue(budget["sufficient"])
            c19 = [item for item in budget["charges"] if item["request_id"] == "REQ-C19"]
            self.assertEqual(len(c19), 1)
            self.assertEqual(c19[0]["charged_cents"], charge)

    def with_tables(self, transform):
        original = Sources.table
        def changed(sources, name):
            rows = deepcopy(original(sources, name))
            transform(name, rows)
            return rows
        with patch.object(Sources, "table", changed):
            return inspect(MANIFEST, SUBJECTS)

    def test_real_budget_deficit_holds_dependent_work_without_forging_authority(self):
        def transform(name, rows):
            if name == "Budget":
                rows[0]["Allocation or commitment (EUR)"] = 5000
        result = self.with_tables(transform)
        c01 = result["batches"][0]["claims"]["C01"]
        self.assertFalse(c01["current_recheck_supported"])
        self.assertTrue(c01["authority"]["current"])
        self.assertIn("shared_budget", {issue["code"] for issue in c01["issues"]})

    def test_unadmitted_conflicting_commitment_creates_real_shared_budget_uncertainty(self):

                rows.append({**original, "Arrival batch": 3, "Obligation (EUR)": 99999, "_ref": "isolated-fixture:conflict"})
        result = self.with_tables(transform)

        result = self.with_tables(transform)
        c19 = result["batches"][3]["claims"]["C19"]

        self.assertEqual(c19["finance"]["net_paid_cents"], 8000)
        self.assertIn("paid_evidence", {issue["code"] for issue in c19["issues"]})

    def test_wrong_cancellation_reference_does_not_waive_current_finding(self):
        sources = Sources(MANIFEST)

        with patch("travel_expense_claim.recheck.claim_versions", return_value=versions):

        self.assertTrue(issue["blocking"])

name: brainstorming
description: "You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation)."
---

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.
